decisions.reason: Attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's node-gyp configure build install script, pulled by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl@0.1.3-alpha.1, failing on missing Windows VS/MSVC — not pnpm or network unreliability.

Shows the top-level static flock import forces fs-ext to load on Windows before branch selection, so --ignore-scripts only relocates the failure to a silent boot-time load error and cannot achieve a working service boot.

Distinguishes Windows acquireLockHandleWin32/CreateSemaphoreW named-semaphore path (no lock file, no flock call) from POSIX flock; concludes the fs-ext binary is dead code on Windows so a load-only stub is safe while Windows locking stays on the semaphore.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: conditional install script skipping node-gyp on win32 only, entry rewritten to a guarded load exporting a compatible flock surface, registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml with lockfile note, plus install/module-load/service-boot and POSIX regression checks.

Explicitly respects the owner's no-Visual-Studio constraint (VS install listed only as a rejected alternative) and uses the repository-managed pnpm patch while stating the published tarball is untouched.
Connects the version-derived DSH-0.1.3-A1 prefix to the fs-ext failure and patch plan and honestly flags the uncertainty, but never cites the full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03.

caps.reason: Installing VS appears only as a rejected alternative; the plan installs nothing.
--ignore-scripts is analyzed and rejected; the plan makes the entry loadable, not merely unbuilt.
Uses the repository's patchedDependencies mechanism; explicitly does not modify the upstream repo or published package.
Windows semaphore path and POSIX flock both remain real; the stub only serves dead Windows code and throws loudly if ever called.
